missions.title: Cantor's Diagonal Construction and Constructive Non-Surjectivity
missions.summary: Constructive diagonal sequence synthesis on binary streams (Nat → Bool) producing an explicit discrepancy index n for every candidate row enum n.

missions.title: Lorenzen's Constructive Lattice-Ordered Divisibility Fragment
missions.summary: Constructive additive and meet/join order laws from Lorenzen's 1951 investigation of lattice-ordered divisibility cones, including additive order cancellation and relative primality.

missions.title: Certifying Algorithms: String Matching & Non-Occurrence Witness Verification
missions.summary: Executable witness checkers and mismatch/non-occurrence certificates following McConnell-Mehlhorn-Näher-Schweitzer (2011 §2 & §9.5), importing Mission H01's promoted Cantor discrepancy theorem to certify universal pattern-table falsifiers.

statement_packages.title: Cantor (1891/1892): Constructive Binary Stream Diagonalization
source_citations: Cantor (1891 lecture / 1892 volume), pp. 75-76: Binary alphabet (m, w) sequences E_1, E_2, ... and diagonal sequence E_0 = (b_1, b_2, ...).
Cantor (1891/1892), p. 76: Pointwise discrepancy b_nu != a_{nu, nu} refuting that E_0 is in the enumeration.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Cantor.flip
declarations.source_ref: p. 75-76 (choice of b_nu distinct from a_{nu,nu})
declarations.back_translation: Given a binary symbol b in {false, true}, returns the opposite symbol via constructive Bool recursion.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Cantor.diagonal
declarations.back_translation: Given an enumeration enum : Nat -> (Nat -> Bool) of binary streams, constructs the diagonal stream n |-> flip (enum n n).

declarations.name: TNDLib.Cantor.DiscrepancyAt
declarations.back_translation: Asserts that binary stream f differs from binary stream g at coordinate n specifically by taking the flipped value f n = flip (g n).

declarations.name: TNDLib.Cantor.DiscrepancyWitness
declarations.source_ref: p. 76 (comparison of E_0 with row E_nu at coordinate nu)
declarations.back_translation: Asserts that candidate stream differs from row enum n at diagonal index n.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Cantor.flip_ne_self
declarations.source_ref: p. 75-76 (mutual exclusivity of m and w)
declarations.back_translation: For every boolean value b, flip b = b entails a contradiction.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Cantor.diagonalDiscrepancy
declarations.back_translation: For every enumeration enum and row index n, the diagonal stream satisfies DiscrepancyWitness enum (diagonal enum) n.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Cantor.diagonal_differ_at
declarations.source_ref: p. 76 (E_0 differs from E_nu in the nu-th coordinate)
declarations.back_translation: For every enumeration enum and index n, diagonal enum n = enum n n is impossible, hence diagonal enum cannot equal row enum n.

declarations.name: TNDTask.cantorFlipInvolution
declarations.back_translation: Open task: Flipping any boolean value twice restores the original boolean value: flip (flip b) = b.

statement_packages.title: Lorenzen (1950/1951): Constructive Lattice-Ordered Divisibility Cone Fragment
source_citations: Lorenzen (1950 submission / 1951 JSL), §1, pp. 81-83: Preordered abelian divisibility cone, cancellation, and greatest-common-divisor / least-common-multiple lattice operations.
Lorenzen (1950/1951), §1, pp. 83-86: Constructive meet/join bounds and relative primality (Teilerfremdheit) x <= a -> x <= b -> x <= 0.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.LOrder
declarations.source_ref: §1, p. 81 (divisibility preorder a <= b on the positive cone)
declarations.back_translation: Constructive order relation a <= b on the natural-number divisibility cone.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.meet
declarations.source_ref: §1, p. 82 (infimum / greatest common divisor a cap b)
declarations.back_translation: Constructive lattice meet (minimum) of a and b computed by decidable comparison.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.join
declarations.source_ref: §1, p. 82 (supremum / least common multiple a cup b)
declarations.back_translation: Constructive lattice join (maximum) of a and b computed by decidable comparison.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.RelPrime
declarations.back_translation: Elements a and b are relatively prime in the cone order when every common lower bound x of a and b is bounded above by 0.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.lorder_of_eq_left
declarations.source_ref: §1, p. 81 (compatibility of cone order with left equality substitution)
declarations.back_translation: If x = y and y <= z in the cone order, then x <= z.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.lorder_of_eq_right
declarations.source_ref: §1, p. 81 (compatibility of cone order with right equality substitution)
declarations.back_translation: If x <= y and z = y in the cone order, then x <= z.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.orderCancelLeft
declarations.source_ref: §1, p. 81 (translation invariance / cancellation of the cone order)
declarations.back_translation: If c + a <= c + b in the cone order, then a <= b.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.meet_le_left
declarations.back_translation: The meet of a and b is bounded above by the left operand a.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.meet_le_right
declarations.back_translation: The meet of a and b is bounded above by the right operand b.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Lorenzen.le_meet
declarations.back_translation: Any element x bounded above by both a and b is bounded above by meet a b.

declarations.name: TNDTask.lorenzenMeetIdem
declarations.back_translation: Open task: For every a, meet a a = a.

declarations.name: TNDTask.lorenzenMeetComm
declarations.back_translation: Open task: For all a and b, meet a b = meet b a.

declarations.name: TNDTask.lorenzenLeJoinLeft
declarations.back_translation: Open task: The left operand a is bounded above by join a b.

statement_packages.title: McConnell-Mehlhorn-Näher-Schweitzer (2010/2011): String Matching & Stream Discrepancy Certificates
source_citations: McConnell, Mehlhorn, Näher, Schweitzer (2011), §2 (pp. 121-125): Witness predicate W(x, y, w) and executable checker soundness.

McConnell et al. (2011), §9.5 (pp. 142-143): String matching occurrence verification and explicit mismatch-offset non-occurrence certificates, combined with Mission H01 Cantor diagonal falsifier certificates.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Certifying.MatchAt2
declarations.source_ref: §9.5, p. 142 (pattern occurrence specification at position pos)
declarations.back_translation: Propositional specification that a 2-symbol binary pattern (p0, p1) occurs in stream text at position pos: text pos = p0 and text (pos + 1) = p1.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Certifying.checkMatchAt2
declarations.back_translation: Executable boolean checker testing whether text pos = p0 and text (pos + 1) = p1.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Certifying.MismatchWitness2
declarations.back_translation: Explicit certificate that pattern (p0, p1) fails to match text at position pos because either offset 0 disagrees (text pos != p0) or offset 1 disagrees (text (pos + 1) != p1).

declarations.name: TNDLib.Certifying.StreamDiscrepancyCert
declarations.source_ref: §2, p. 122 + Cantor (1891) p. 76 (cross-mission universal table falsifier witness)
declarations.back_translation: Certificate that candidate stream differs from row n of a pattern table at diagonal index n, defined via TNDLib.Cantor.DiscrepancyWitness.

declarations.name: TNDLib.Certifying.diagonalStreamCert
declarations.source_ref: §2.1, p. 122 + Cantor (1891) p. 76 (universal falsifier certificate constructor)
declarations.back_translation: For any infinite table of binary patterns and any row index n, Cantor's diagonal stream produces a valid StreamDiscrepancyCert at row n.

declarations.name: TNDTask.certCheckMatchSound
declarations.back_translation: Open task: If the executable checker checkMatchAt2 text p0 p1 pos returns true, then MatchAt2 text p0 p1 pos holds.

statement_packages.title: Lehmann-Sanders-Walzer (2023/2025): ShockHash Two-Choice & Pseudoforest Orientation Certificates
source_citations: Lehmann, Sanders, Walzer (2023 arXiv / 2025 Algorithmica), §2-§3 (pp. 430-436): Each key i in {0,...,n-1} has two candidate hash slots h_0(i), h_1(i); a 1-bit selector vector s in {0,1}^n chooses a slot for each key.

Lehmann, Sanders, Walzer (2025), §3.1 (pp. 432-435): Viewing candidate pairs as edges of a bipartite/cuckoo graph, a valid Minimal Perfect Hash Function corresponds to a 1-orientation (pseudoforest orientation where every target slot receives in-degree at most 1).

declarations.name: TNDPackage.M02ShockHash.TwoChoiceHash
declarations.source_ref: §2, p. 430 (pair of candidate hash functions h_0, h_1 : [n] -> [m])
declarations.back_translation: A finite two-choice hash table specification mapping each of n keys to two candidate slots h0 i and h1 i in Fin m.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.M02ShockHash.SelectorBits
declarations.back_translation: A boolean selector function Fin n -> Bool choosing between h0 (false) and h1 (true) for each key.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.M02ShockHash.selectedSlot
declarations.back_translation: Evaluates the chosen slot in Fin m for key i under two-choice hash H and selector bit s i.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.M02ShockHash.CollisionFree
declarations.source_ref: §2, p. 430 (injectivity / collision freedom of selected slots)
declarations.back_translation: Asserts that for all keys i and j, if selectedSlot H s i = selectedSlot H s j, then i = j.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.M02ShockHash.PseudoforestOrientationCert
declarations.back_translation: Certificate bundling a selector bit-vector s, a reverse slot-owner map slotOwner : Fin m -> Option (Fin n), and the witness law that every key i is recorded as the unique owner of its selected slot.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.M02ShockHash.orientation_cert_implies_collision_free
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: Any TwoChoiceHash equipped with a valid PseudoforestOrientationCert is collision-free (injective on Fin n).

declarations.name: TNDPackage.M02ShockHash.CollisionFreePair2
declarations.back_translation: Specializes collision freedom to two keys with selected slots slot0 and slot1, asserting slot0 != slot1.

statement_packages.title: Schönfinkel (1920/1924): Typed Combinators I, C, T, Z, S and Reductions to C and S
source_citations: Schönfinkel (1920 lecture / 1924 Math. Ann.), §2, p. 306: Representation of multi-argument functions by single-argument higher-order functions (currying/uncurrying).

Schönfinkel (1924), §3, pp. 308-310: Definitions of Identitätsfunktion I, Konstanzfunktion C (modern K), Vertauschungsfunktion T (modern C), Zusammensetzungsfunktion Z (modern B), and Verschmelzungsfunktion S.
Schönfinkel (1924), §4, pp. 311-312: Reduction of I = S C C, Z = S (C S) C, and T = S (Z Z S) (C C) to C and S alone.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.curry
declarations.source_ref: §2, p. 306 (reduction of binary function f(x, y) to unary function-valued function)
declarations.back_translation: Transforms a function on pairs (alpha x beta) -> gamma into a curried function alpha -> beta -> gamma.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.uncurry
declarations.source_ref: §2, p. 306 (inverse passage from unary higher-order function to binary function)
declarations.back_translation: Transforms a curried function alpha -> beta -> gamma into a function on pairs (alpha x beta) -> gamma.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.combI
declarations.back_translation: Schönfinkel's identity combinator I : alpha -> alpha.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.combC
declarations.source_ref: §3, p. 309, eq. (2): (C x) y = x (modern K combinator)
declarations.back_translation: Schönfinkel's constancy combinator C : alpha -> beta -> alpha returning its first argument.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.combT
declarations.source_ref: §3, p. 309, eq. (3): (T f) x y = f y x (modern C combinator)
declarations.back_translation: Schönfinkel's argument-swapping combinator (Vertauschungsfunktion) T.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.combZ
declarations.source_ref: §3, p. 310, eq. (4): Z f g x = f (g x) (modern B combinator)
declarations.back_translation: Schönfinkel's composition combinator (Zusammensetzungsfunktion) Z.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.combS
declarations.back_translation: Schönfinkel's fusion combinator (Verschmelzungsfunktion) S.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.schoenfinkel_I_from_CS
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: Evaluating S C C on any argument x yields I x = x.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.schoenfinkel_Z_from_CS
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: Pointwise reduction of composition Z f g x to S (C S) C f g x.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L01Schoenfinkel.schoenfinkel_T_from_CSZ
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: Pointwise reduction of swap T f x y to S (Z Z S) (C C) f x y.

statement_packages.title: Ackermann (1927/1928): Original 3-Variable Hierarchy phi(a, b, n)
source_citations: Ackermann (1927 submission / 1928 Math. Ann.), pp. 119-120: Initial value function alpha(a, n) = 0 (n=0), 1 (n=1), a (n>=2) and 3-variable recursion phi(a, b, n).
Ackermann (1928), p. 119: Explicit level-0 (a + b), level-1 (a * b), and level-2 (iterated multiplication with base a at b=0) characterizations.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L03Ackermann.ackAlpha
declarations.back_translation: Ackermann's base-value helper: returns 0 when n = 0, 1 when n = 1, and a when n >= 2.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L03Ackermann.ackPhi
declarations.source_ref: p. 120 (simultaneous recursion for phi(a, b, n))
declarations.back_translation: Ackermann's original 3-argument hierarchy phi(a, b, n): at level 0 returns a + b; at level n + 1 returns ackAlpha a n when b = 0 and ackPhi a (ackPhi a b' n + 1) n when b = b' + 1.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L03Ackermann.ackPhi_level0
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: At level n = 0, Ackermann's phi(a, b, 0) equals a + b.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L03Ackermann.ackPhi_level1_zero
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: At level n = 1 and b = 0, phi(a, 0, 1) = 0.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L03Ackermann.ackPhi_level2_zero
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: At level n = 2 and b = 0, phi(a, 0, 2) = 1.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L03Ackermann.ackPhi_level3_zero
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: At level n = 3 and b = 0, phi(a, 0, 3) = a, capturing Ackermann's non-standard base convention for n >= 3.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.L03Ackermann.AckLevel1Spec
declarations.back_translation: Target specification stating that phi(a, b, 1) equals the product a * b for all a, b.

statement_packages.title: Perron (1951/1952): Proof of Moessner's Theorem via Prefix Sums and Binomial Coefficients
source_citations: Perron (1951 lecture / 1952 BadW Sitzungsberichte), pp. 31-32: Definition of Moessner's sieve by dropping every k-th term and forming partial sums.
Perron (1951/1952), pp. 32-34: Binomial-coefficient representation of intermediate rows and derivation of k-th powers n^k.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H08PerronMoessner.prefixSum
declarations.source_ref: p. 31 (partial sum operator on sequence terms)
declarations.back_translation: Computes the partial sum f 0 + f 1 + ... + f (n - 1) of a natural-number sequence.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H08PerronMoessner.oddTerm
declarations.source_ref: p. 31 (sequence 1, 3, 5, ... remaining after deleting every 2nd positive integer)
declarations.back_translation: Returns the k-th odd positive integer 2 * k + 1 (0-indexed).

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H08PerronMoessner.binom
declarations.source_ref: p. 32 (Pascal binomial coefficients used in Perron's induction)
declarations.back_translation: Standard recursive definition of binomial coefficient C(n, k) on Nat.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H08PerronMoessner.pascal_step
declarations.source_ref: p. 32 (Pascal recurrence C(n+1, k+1) = C(n, k) + C(n, k+1))
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: Binomial coefficients satisfy Pascal's additive recurrence.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H08PerronMoessner.moessner_rank2_step
declarations.source_ref: p. 31 (rank-2 Moessner step: prefix sum of odd numbers steps by 2n + 1)
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: prefixSum oddTerm (n + 1) = prefixSum oddTerm n + (2 * n + 1).

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H08PerronMoessner.MoessnerRank2Squares
declarations.source_ref: p. 31 (rank-2 case of Moessner's theorem: sum of first n odd numbers is n^2)
declarations.back_translation: Target specification that prefixSum oddTerm n = n * n for all n.

statement_packages.title: Sperner (1927/1928): Subset Antichains and Middle Binomial Coefficient Bound
source_citations: Sperner (1927 submission / 1928 Math. Z.), p. 544: System of subsets of an n-element set in which no subset contains another (antichain) has cardinality at most C(n, floor(n/2)).
Sperner (1928), pp. 545-546: Layer shift / shade construction and binomial bound.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H03Sperner.BitSubset
declarations.source_ref: p. 544 (subset of an n-element ground set)
declarations.back_translation: Represents a subset of {0, ..., n - 1} by its characteristic function Fin n -> Bool.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H03Sperner.SubsetLe
declarations.back_translation: Pointwise inclusion of bitvector subsets: every element i with A i = true also satisfies B i = true.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H03Sperner.Incomparable
declarations.source_ref: p. 544 (neither subset is contained in the other)
declarations.back_translation: Two subsets A and B are incomparable when neither A subseteq B nor B subseteq A holds.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H03Sperner.PairwiseAntichain
declarations.back_translation: Inductive predicate asserting that a list of subsets has all distinct pairs incomparable (which also forces duplicate-freedom).

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H03Sperner.middleBinom
declarations.back_translation: Computes the middle binomial coefficient C(n, n / 2).

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H03Sperner.SpernerBoundSpec
declarations.source_ref: p. 544, Satz (main upper bound |F| <= C(n, floor(n/2)))
declarations.back_translation: Target specification: For every list F of subsets of Fin n satisfying PairwiseAntichain F, F.length <= middleBinom n.

declarations.name: TNDPackage.H03Sperner.singleton_antichain_bound
declarations.source_ref: p. 544 (non-vacuity and base-case verification for singleton families)
declarations.back_translation: Proved theorem: Any 1-element family [A] is a valid PairwiseAntichain and satisfies [A].length <= middleBinom n.
